introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0550 Geography 1, June 2025, Ordinary Level), General Certificate of Education Board. Duration: one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; choose only one answer for each question. If you mark more than one answer you score zero for that question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Use a soft HB pencil on the answer sheet.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Answer all 50 questions.
incertitudes: Sujet sans couche texte (scan), lu en image page par page : aucune figure, carte ni schema dans ce Paper 1 (la liste de la question 5 est du texte), donc aucune figure produite. Aucune cle officielle n'est imprimee : toutes les reponses sont deduites du programme.

Question 6 (preuve la plus convaincante de la forme de la Terre) : options ambigues (des photographies aeriennes ne montrent pas la forme de la Terre, la circumnavigation ne prouve pas seule la sphericite). Convertie en question ouverte, aucune lettre choisie.
Question 20 (facteur du developpement du sol) : la temperature fait partie du climat, elle n'est pas un facteur distinct dans la liste classique ; retenu B. Sujet discutable.
Question 22 (plantes vertes) : formulation imparfaite ("generate all energy") ; seule option decrivant le role de producteur, retenu A.
Question 31 : "market gardening" retenu ; "horticulture" (B) est le terme plus large, ce qui rend le sujet un peu discutable.
Question 49 : "watershed" employe pour la zone d'origine du Sanaga ; retenu Adamawa Highlands (C), formulation du sujet imprecise.
Question 8 : l'equinoxe du 21 mars est le printemps dans l'hemisphere nord (automne dans l'hemisphere sud) ; retenu B, convention du sujet.

Fautes d'impression conservees dans les enonces et options : "Foot harvest" (post-harvest), "Trilise" (trellis), "inha" (inhabitants), "compose of", "Cost more rain to fall" (Q19), "jewelries". Aucun calcul numerique important ; les seuls calculs (echelle 2 cm pour 1 km = 1:50 000, 360/24 = 15 degres, 60/10 = 6) sont recalcules avec Python.

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 17, 18, 32. Q17 : B (environmental protection) et D (resource conservation) sont deux avantages reels. Q18 : A (fog) et C (desert conditions) sont deux effets reels de courants froids. Q32 : C est une hypothese de Von Thunen, D en est le resultat predit ; D retenu comme visee habituelle.

questions.enonce_markdown: The scale of a map expressed as 2 cm to 1 km is a
questions.corrige_markdown: A scale written in words, such as "2 cm represent 1 km", is a **statement scale** (also called a verbal scale). Check: 1 km = 100 000 cm, so 2 cm : 100 000 cm = 1 : 50 000, which is what a ratio scale or Representative Fraction would show as numbers (1:50 000). A linear scale is a drawn line divided into units. The trap is to choose A or B because the same scale could also be written as 1:50 000; the form given in the question is words. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An area with closely spaced contour lines indicates:
questions.corrige_markdown: Contour lines join points of equal height. When they are close together, the height changes quickly over a short horizontal distance, so the slope is **steep**. Widely spaced contours show a gentle slope, and evenly spaced contours show a uniform (even) slope. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A six figure grid reference gives:
questions.corrige_markdown: A four figure reference only names a whole grid square (an area of 1 km by 1 km on a 1:50 000 map). A six figure reference divides each square into tenths in both the Eastings and the Northings, so it fixes the **exact location** of a feature to within about 100 m. It gives no direction (that is a bearing) and the word "situation" in geography refers to the position of a settlement relative to its surroundings. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The exact location of a feature.
The area of location of a feature.
The direction of location of a feature.
The situation of location of a feature.

questions.enonce_markdown: The presence of residence on a map is an indication of
questions.corrige_markdown: Houses and other places where people live are shown on a map as buildings or built-up areas, and this land use is called **settlement (residential) land use**. Industrial, recreational and waste land uses are shown by factories, parks or sports grounds and dumps. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the following land uses on a landscape and answer question 5.

**(i) Sand Pit (ii) Caravan Site (iii) Police Station (iv) View Point (v) Parking.**

Which of the combinations of land uses indicates the tourist services of the settlement?
questions.corrige_markdown: Tourist services are facilities that serve visitors: a **caravan site** (accommodation), a **view point** (attraction) and **parking** (for visitors' vehicles), that is (ii), (iv) and (v). A sand pit is an extractive land use and a police station is an administrative or security service, neither is specifically for tourists. This eliminates A, B and D, which all contain (i) or (iii). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The most convincing proof for the shape of the earth is

*Options as printed:* A) Aerial photographs.   B) Circumnavigation.   C) Ship's visibility.   D) Circular Horizon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
This question has no single reliable key, so it is left open for self-assessment. Evidence that the Earth is spherical includes: the hull of a ship disappearing before its mast as it sails away; the round shadow of the Earth on the Moon during a lunar eclipse; different time zones; the circular horizon seen from a height; circumnavigation; and photographs of the whole Earth taken from space by satellites and astronauts. The most direct and convincing proof today is a photograph of the whole Earth taken from space, which shows its round shape directly. Of the options printed, "Aerial photographs" taken from an aircraft show only a small part of the surface and cannot show the shape of the Earth (unless the examiners meant satellite photographs), while circumnavigation, ship's visibility and the circular horizon are the classic textbook evidences, each of them only a partial proof (a journey around the Earth does not by itself prove it is a sphere rather than, say, a cylinder). A candidate who explains the strongest proof and its limits has answered the question well.

No letter is imposed: the printed wording makes the options open to dispute, so the question is not auto-marked.
themes: evidence for the earth's spherical shape

questions.enonce_markdown: Russia and the USA have more than one time zone because they
questions.corrige_markdown: The Earth turns through 360 degrees in 24 hours, so it turns 360 / 24 = $15^{\circ}$ of longitude each hour, and one standard time zone covers about $15^{\circ}$ of longitude. A country that extends over much more than $15^{\circ}$ from east to west, like Russia or the USA, therefore needs several time zones. Latitude (north-south extent) does not affect clock time, and neither Russia nor the USA lies across the equator. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Spread across more than $15^{\circ}$ of longitudes.
Spread across more than $15^{\circ}$ of latitudes.

questions.enonce_markdown: During the revolution of the earth (on its orbit), the date 21st March indicates:
questions.corrige_markdown: On about 21 March the Sun is overhead at the equator, day and night are equal everywhere, and this is the **Spring (vernal) Equinox** in the northern hemisphere. The solstices occur on about 21 June and 22 December and the autumn equinox on about 23 September. (In the southern hemisphere the same date is the autumn equinox, but the usual textbook convention names it from the northern hemisphere.) **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following are components of the hydrological cycle:

**(i) Soil Moisture (ii) Precipitation (iii) Runoff (iv) Ground Water**

Which of the combinations represents only stores in the hydrological cycle?
questions.corrige_markdown: In the hydrological cycle a **store** is a place where water is held (for example the oceans, ice, lakes, soil moisture and groundwater), while a **flow** or transfer is water on the move (precipitation, runoff, evaporation, infiltration). Soil moisture (i) and groundwater (iv) are stores. Precipitation (ii) and runoff (iii) are flows, so options B, C and D each contain a flow. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The lateral movement of water within the zone of permanent saturation and rocks is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: The zone of permanent saturation is the water table and the saturated rock below it (groundwater). Water moving sideways through it towards a river channel is **base flow** (groundwater flow). Through flow is lateral movement in the soil above the water table, percolation is the downward movement of water through soil and rock, and infiltration is the entry of water into the soil surface. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The stratosphere is an important layer of the atmosphere because
questions.corrige_markdown: The stratosphere contains the **ozone layer**, which absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun and so protects living things. Water vapour and weather belong to the troposphere, and in the stratosphere temperature rises with height (because of the ozone), it does not fall. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Rainfall is measured with a rain gauge and recorded in millimetres while cloud cover is
questions.corrige_markdown: Cloud cover is estimated by eye: the observer judges how many eighths of the sky are covered, and the unit is the **okta** (0 to 8 oktas). A hygrometer measures humidity, a barometer measures air pressure (millibars) and the Campbell-Stokes recorder measures hours of sunshine. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Measured by eye observation and recorded in oktas.
Measured by hygrometer and recorded in percentages.
Measured by barometer and recorded in millibars.
Measured by Campbell Stokes and recorded in hours.

questions.enonce_markdown: The process by which all forms of condensation fall back to the earth surface is
questions.corrige_markdown: Water droplets and ice crystals formed by condensation fall to the ground as rain, snow, sleet, hail or drizzle. This process is **precipitation**. Evaporation is the change from liquid to vapour, saturation is when the air holds all the water vapour it can, and sublimation is the change between solid and gas without a liquid stage. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The prevailing wind blowing over Cameroon that is associated with the rainy season is:
questions.corrige_markdown: In Cameroon the rainy season is brought by the moist **south-west monsoon** (tropical maritime air from the Atlantic Ocean) when the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone moves north. The harmattan is the dry, dusty north-east trade wind of the dry season. Hurricanes and cyclones are tropical storms, not prevailing winds, and they do not affect Cameroon. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Inland areas have high diurnal temperature ranges because of:
questions.corrige_markdown: The diurnal range is the difference between the day maximum and the night minimum. Land heats up and cools down quickly, whereas the sea does so slowly. Places far from the sea, away from its moderating effect, therefore have large daily ranges: this effect is called **continentality**. Insolation affects how hot the day is but it does not by itself explain the large range, and ocean currents affect coasts, not inland areas. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mountains modify climate in that as height increases
questions.corrige_markdown: As altitude increases the air becomes thinner, so **air pressure falls**. Temperature also falls with height (the normal lapse rate is about 6.5 degrees Celsius per 1000 m), so C is wrong, and wind speeds usually increase rather than reduce on exposed high ground. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
One importance of waste management are:

*Options as printed:* A) Free flow of surface runoff.   B) Environmental protection.   C) Soil contamination.   D) Resource conservation.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Proper collection, treatment and disposal of waste prevents pollution of water, soil and air and protects health, so **environmental protection** is an importance of waste management. Soil contamination (C) and blocked drains and runoff (A) are problems caused by poor waste management. Resource conservation (D, through recycling and reuse) is also a real benefit, which is why this question is left open.

**Intended answer: B (Environmental protection).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
One of the effects of cold ocean currents on the climates of adjacent landmasses is that it causes:

*Options as printed:* A) Fog development.   B) Abundant rainfall.   C) Desert conditions.   D) Severe winters.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cold currents (for example the Benguela Current off south-west Africa and the Peru Current off Chile) cool the air above them. Cool air holds little water vapour and is stable, so it does not rise and form rain clouds. Winds blowing onto the land bring dry air and the coast becomes arid, giving **desert conditions** such as the Namib and Atacama deserts. Fog does form along these coasts, but the typical effect on the climate of the adjacent land is aridity. Abundant rainfall is caused by warm currents, and severe winters are not an effect of cold currents.

**Intended answer: C (Desert conditions).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The best way to solve problems of water shortages is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Dams store water in reservoirs during the wet season so that it can be supplied for homes, irrigation and industry in the dry season. People cannot make more rain fall (B) or increase the number of rivers (C), and raising the price of water (A) reduces use but does not supply more water. **Construct dams.** **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the aspect below which is not a factor of soil development.
questions.corrige_markdown: The factors of soil formation in the usual textbook list are parent rock, **climate**, relief, living organisms (including **vegetation**) and **time**. Temperature is not listed as a separate factor because it is one element of climate. So the option that is not a factor in its own right is Temperature. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Evergreen trees, continuous canopies, multiple layers, are characteristics of the
questions.corrige_markdown: The tropical rainforest has tall broad-leaved evergreen trees that shed leaves at different times, a continuous canopy and several layers (emergents, canopy, understorey and shrub layer). Monsoon forests are deciduous in the dry season, coniferous forests have needle-leaved trees of cold regions, and mangrove forests grow in salty coastal swamps. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Green plants are considered very important in the ecosystems because they:
questions.corrige_markdown: Green plants are the **producers**: by photosynthesis they change the Sun's light energy into chemical energy in food, which is the starting point of every food chain. Breaking down dead material is the work of decomposers, and plants do not feed on other organisms or depend on all organisms. Option A is imperfectly worded (plants do not generate energy, they capture and store it), but it is the only one that describes their role. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The layer of the earth's interior compose of the sial and sima is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: The crust is made of two parts: the lighter **sial** (silica and aluminium, forming the continents) and the denser **sima** (silica and magnesium, forming the ocean floor). The mantle lies below it and the outer and inner cores (nife) lie deeper. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Rocks that are formed from the remains of living and non-living things are called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sedimentary rocks form when sediments (rock fragments, and the remains of plants and animals such as shells) are deposited in layers and compacted and cemented. Examples are sandstone, limestone and coal. Volcanic and plutonic rocks are igneous (from cooled magma) and metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an aspect of physical weathering?
questions.corrige_markdown: Physical (mechanical) weathering breaks rock without changing its chemistry, for example **frost action** (freeze-thaw), where water freezes in cracks and expands. Hydrolysis, hydration and carbonation are all chemical weathering processes. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: It is not a practical strategy for preserving life in the event of a volcanic eruption:
questions.corrige_markdown: Evacuation centres, exclusion zones around the volcano and coordination of the emergency services all help to save lives. Building tall concrete buildings does not protect people from lava, ash falls or pyroclastic flows, so it is **not** a practical strategy. The question asks for the option that is not practical. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Construction of tall and concrete building.

questions.enonce_markdown: A drainage pattern in which the tributaries meet the main river at acute angles forming a tree-like pattern describes:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **dendritic** pattern (from the Greek word for tree) looks like the branches of a tree, with tributaries joining the main river at acute angles. It develops on rock of uniform resistance. A radial pattern flows outwards from a central high point, an annular pattern forms rings around a dome, and the trellis pattern (printed as "Trilise") has tributaries joining at right angles. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a challenge in adopting climate smart agriculture?
questions.corrige_markdown: Livestock management, post-harvest management (printed "Foot harvest") and conservation agriculture are practices used in climate smart agriculture. A challenge in adopting it is the set of obstacles farmers face, such as **market barriers** (poor access to markets and fair prices), together with cost, lack of information and credit. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Development that considers the needs of all the people today and those still to come is
questions.corrige_markdown: This is the definition of **sustainable development**: development that meets the needs of the present without reducing the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the list of farming types that are practised in areas with abundant farmland.
questions.corrige_markdown: Where land is plentiful, farmers can use large areas with few inputs per hectare, which is extensive farming: **ranching, shifting cultivation and plantation** farming. Dairy farming and battery hen farming (A), wet paddy and horticulture (B) and viticulture and market gardening (C) are intensive, using small areas with heavy inputs. C also contains bush fallowing, but the other two items are intensive, so only D is a list made wholly of farming types suited to abundant land. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most common example of intensive commercial farming is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Intensive commercial farming uses a small area, much labour and capital, and produces crops for sale. The most common example is **market gardening**: vegetables and fruit grown near towns for urban markets. Horticulture is the wider term, viticulture is the growing of grapes only, and mixed farming (crops and livestock together) is not necessarily intensive. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
One main assumption of Von Thünen's model on agricultural land use patterns is that:

*Options as printed:* A) There are many markets on the landscape.   B) Extensive farming is near the city while intensive is far away.   C) Transport types and cost in the area are the same.   D) Intensive farming is near the city while extensive is far away
questions.corrige_markdown:
Von Thünen's model assumes an isolated state with **one** central market, a flat plain with uniform soil and climate, one type of transport, and transport cost that rises with distance. Option C is therefore a genuine assumption of the model and A is false (there is only one market). Option D states the land use pattern that the model **predicts** (intensive farming near the city, extensive farming far away) and B reverses it. Since C is an assumption and D is the result, the question is left open; the pattern in D is the answer usually expected.

**Intended answer: D (Intensive farming is near the city while extensive is far away).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are referred to as energy for the future: (i) Coal (ii) Solar energy (iii) natural gas (iv) HEP
questions.corrige_markdown: Energy for the future means sources that will not run out, the renewable sources: **solar energy (ii)** and **hydro-electric power, HEP (iv)**. Coal (i) and natural gas (iii) are fossil fuels, which are non-renewable and will be exhausted. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following industries are all examples of light industry? (i) Brewery industry (ii) Petrochemical industry (iii) Dairy factory (iv) Metallurgical industry (v) Canneries.
questions.corrige_markdown: Light industries make small consumer goods from light raw materials, often food and drink: the **brewery (i), dairy factory (iii) and canneries (v)**. The petrochemical industry (ii) and the metallurgical industry (iv) are heavy industries that process bulky raw materials such as crude oil and ores. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is not a strategy to improve industrialisation in the LICS?
questions.corrige_markdown: A stable banking system, tax holidays for foreign investors and a peaceful, conducive political climate all attract capital and help industry to grow in Low Income Countries (LICs). Moving industries away from their existing sites does nothing to increase industrialisation, so it is **not** a strategy. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Movement of industries from existing sites.
Provide tax holidays for overseas investors.

questions.enonce_markdown: Cheese, butter, wool, linen, watches and jewelries are products of the:
questions.corrige_markdown: Cheese and butter (dairy), wool and linen (textiles), and watches and jewellery are small, light consumer goods, which are products of **light industry**. The list also includes non-food items, so option C (food processing) is too narrow. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Industries are considered as raw material oriented when the material index is:
questions.corrige_markdown: In Weber's theory the **material index** = weight of localised raw materials / weight of the finished product. If the index is greater than 1, the raw material loses weight in processing, so it is cheaper to put the factory near the raw material: the industry is raw material oriented. If it is less than 1 the industry is market oriented, and if it is equal to 1 it is footloose (it can be located anywhere between the two). Example: if 5 tonnes of sugar cane give 1 tonne of sugar, the index is 5 / 1 = 5, which is greater than 1. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Heavy industries are few in the developing countries mainly because of
questions.corrige_markdown: Heavy industries (steel, shipbuilding, petrochemicals) need very large sums of money for plant and machinery. Developing countries generally lack this **capital**, so it is the main reason. Technology, skilled labour and transport are also problems but they follow from, or are less decisive than, the shortage of capital. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The greatest advantage of water transport over the other modes of transport is that it is
questions.corrige_markdown: Ships and barges can carry very large quantities of heavy, bulky goods (oil, ores, grain, containers) at low cost per tonne, so water transport is a **bulk carrier**. It is the least flexible (it needs ports and waterways) and the slowest of the modes, so A and D are wrong. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The unfavourable trade balance of the Less Economically Developed Countries is because of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Less Economically Developed Countries mostly export primary products whose prices are low and unstable, but import expensive manufactured goods. These **unfair terms of trade** make the value of imports greater than the value of exports, producing an unfavourable (negative) trade balance. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Examples of high population density areas in the world are the
questions.corrige_markdown: Densely populated regions are those with a favourable climate, fertile land, industry and long settlement, such as **Western Europe and South-East Asia** (and the Nile valley, the Ganges plain, eastern China). Mountains, deserts and tundra are harsh, sparsely populated areas. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Western Europe and south East Asia.

questions.enonce_markdown: The natural change of a population is determined by
questions.corrige_markdown: Natural change (natural increase) = birth rate minus death rate. Migration is a separate component, so options that contain migrants or emigrants and immigrants are wrong. The answer is **births and deaths**. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Under population occurs when resources are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Under-population exists when a country has more resources than its population can use. The resources are **more than the population** and the country could support more people at a higher standard of living. Equal resources and population describe the optimum population, and resources less than the population describe over-population. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The location of a settlement relative to its environment is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: The **situation** of a settlement is its position in relation to the surrounding area (for example near a river crossing, a road junction or a coast). The site is the actual piece of land on which the settlement is built, the form is its shape, and the pattern is the way settlements are arranged (dispersed, nucleated or linear). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The largest unit of a settlement on the landscape is
questions.corrige_markdown: Settlements are ranked by size in the urban hierarchy: hamlet, village, town, city, conurbation, megacity. Among the options, the **megacity** (a city of more than ten million people) is the largest. Hamlets and villages are small rural settlements and a town is smaller than a city. **Answer: D.**
themes: urban hierarchy and rank size rule

questions.enonce_markdown: Conservation of natural resources refers to
questions.corrige_markdown: Conservation is the careful and sensible management of resources so that they last and are available to future generations: **wise use**. It does not mean never using them (that is preservation), nor stockpiling them, nor using them up. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In Cameroon, if some regions have population density of less than 10 inha/km² while others have above 60 inha/km², what does this tell about population distribution in the country?
questions.corrige_markdown: Density is the number of inhabitants per square kilometre. The same country has areas with fewer than 10 inha/km² (very low) and areas with more than 60 inha/km² (at least six times higher), so people are concentrated in some regions and almost absent from others: the distribution is **highly uneven**. If it were even, all regions would have similar densities. Note: 60 / 10 = 6, so the denser regions have at least six times the density of the sparse ones. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main climatic types of Cameroon are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Cameroon lies between about 2 and 13 degrees north of the equator. The south has the **equatorial** climate (rain all year) and the north has the **tropical** climate (a long dry season and a shorter wet season). The Adamawa plateau and the western highlands modify these types with altitude, but there is no temperate or true monsoon climate type. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The watershed of the Sanaga River in Cameroon is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The Sanaga, one of the longest rivers wholly in Cameroon, is formed by the meeting of the Lom and the Djerem, whose headwaters lie on the **Adamawa Highlands**. The Adamawa plateau is the great divide that separates the rivers flowing south to the Atlantic Ocean (such as the Sanaga) from those flowing north to the Benue and Lake Chad basins. Mount Cameroon, the Rumpi Hills and the Mandara Mountains do not form the Sanaga basin. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Food waste refers to a situation where:
questions.corrige_markdown: Food waste is edible food thrown away at the end of the chain by retailers, restaurants and households, that is, **food disposal at home and in restaurants**. Food that is lost before it reaches the market (D, for example because of bad roads or poor storage) is called food loss. A and B do not describe waste. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Food is prepared far from consumers.
Food is served to a large population.
Food disposal occurs at home and restaurants.
Food does not reach the market because of bad roads.
